findings.title: Explicit null accounting blocks are mistaken for absent legacy blocks
findings.retires: The build’s claimed closure of #203’s requirement that one of time and cost without the other is a disagreement.
findings.rejection_test: test_doctor_rejects_null_time_without_cost: seal a statement carrying "time": null and no cost; proof six must fail and name item 1 and time.
findings.severity: Blocking when a sealed statement carries either accounting key with null: proof six incorrectly holds instead of rejecting the carried invalid accounting.

findings.title: Float coercion makes distinct large numbers compare equal
findings.retires: The build’s claim that accounting numbers are compared exactly, with no tolerance.
findings.rejection_test: test_doctor_rejects_large_integer_that_rounds_to_summed_float: records sum to 9007199254740992.0, while the sealed statement says 9007199254740993; proof six must fail and name the field.
findings.severity: Blocking once an accounting value reaches the IEEE-754 integer precision boundary: a one-unit disagreement can satisfy proof six.
